descriptions.description: Mahogany, obtained from several species in the genus Swietenia, is regarded as the world’s finest timber for high-class furniture and cabinet work. This species was the first to be discovered by the Europeans and has been exported from Hispaniola since the 16th century. It has been widely over-exploited in the wild and is now cultivated in plantations in other areas of the tropics. It is grown as an ornamental tree in various parts of India.

This species is one of the secondary sources of a very popular Arab dye called 'waras', 'wars' or 'warus. Waras is a coarse purple or brilliant orange-brown powder. The plant is sometimes cultivated for green manure, to provide shade for plantations and to stabilize the soil.
